Once a qualifying item is visibly confirmed and all newer orders plus every same-date row have been checked, copy the full displayed “Order Date,” enumerate all tied qualifying orders if applicable, account for status according to the task wording, and provide the answer immediately rather than continuing without a conclusion.

Verify every requested order is visibly present, copy the full displayed status exactly, and do not return an unlabeled list of statuses.

Treat autocomplete suggestions and review-count links as navigation aids rather than evidence; on every pagination click, verify the active page and displayed review range before reading, and resolve any repeated or conflicting rows instead of relying on navigation history.

Enumerate every qualifying reviewer, preserve near-identical name variants exactly, open a detail view if any value is abbreviated, and never include a name inferred from a truncated note or unsupported by visible review text.

Compare the complete product name and variant, and open its detail page if the result is abbreviated or could match a near-identical model.

Convert scales only when the source value and scale are visibly supported, apply the requested rounding afterward, and inspect every qualifying or tied result when multiple exact matches exist.

Advanced Search returns global results and has no category control; instead, use the category page’s visible Price facet, progressively narrow its coarse bands, increase the visible items per page, and inspect every relevant band and page while excluding boundary-priced items that violate strict limits.

reasoning.content: Read each qualifying card or open its product detail page and visibly confirm the full product name, category breadcrumb, displayed price, and rating before acting; enumerate every tied top-rated result rather than stopping at the first candidate. On the detail page, distinguish near-identical variants, select every required option, then use “Add to Cart” and open “My Cart” if needed to verify the exact configured item—not merely a changed cart count.
